You are skeptic #2. A WCAG/§4 audit of Heard's "primitives-shell" screen produced this finding. Independently verify it by READING the cited code. Try to REFUTE it — default to real=false if the code already handles it, the claim is a stylistic nit, or it's not actually reachable by a user.

FILE: /Users/taha/Claude projects/TEWW apps/Therapy (Heard)/app/(provider)/provider/dashboard/page.tsx
LOCATION: Lines 189-227 (StatCard grid for 'At a glance' section)
RULE: 7
TITLE: Stat cards lack section heading pattern — no h3 linking cards to a descriptive title
DETAIL: The 'At a glance' section has an h2 heading (line 187) but does NOT wrap the grid of StatCards in a semantic section or article. The StatCard component renders as a <div>, not a <section>. While the heading is present, the heading-to-content relationship is implicit, not explicit. A screen reader user navigating by heading may not clearly understand that this h2 is a section heading for the 5 stat cards that follow — they may perceive the heading as standalone. The requirements state 'stat cards labeled (number has a text label)', which is satisfied; but the section structure could be clearer.
SUGGESTION: Wrap the StatCard grid in a <section aria-labelledby="glance-heading"> and give the h2 an id="glance-heading". This makes the heading-section relationship explicit to assistive technologies. Alternatively, ensure the h2 has a clear semantic parent or use the Card component with as="section" if applicable.

Return real=true ONLY if this is a genuine, actionable accessibility/polish gap that a fix would meaningfully improve.
